Subject: Azure private listing — governance evidence request and a couple commercial questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — product looked promising. Before we can progress to an internal SOW approval for the Azure private plan, procurement and security have a few asks: 

1) Can you provide a short SOC 2 Type II evidence summary and a pointer to the full report (redacted where appropriate)? Our security team needs to verify scope and any subservice orgs.
2) We need a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones tied to Azure private listing activation and entitlement dates.
3) Commercial: MediCore is requesting a 90-day onboarding credit and a clause for an SLA remedy cap of 3x monthly commitment for the first 6 months — is that something Redwood can accept?

If you can share the items this week, I’ll try to get this in front of finance next Tuesday.

Cheers,

Irene / Marissa — quick read of the asks:

- SOC2: we can share a 2-page summary and a redacted report under an NDA. Standard.
- MAP: legal prefers milestones that de-risk both sides; I’ve sketched items for onboarding, entitlement activation, and joint verification checkpoints.
- SLA remedy cap: 3x monthly commitment as a cap is high on a brand-new private listing. We typically offer service credits capped at 1x monthly fees for initial commercial pilots. For an enterprise with procurement push, we can consider a time-boxed exception if MediCore accepts a shortened warranty window and agrees to a usage/volume commitment and a commitment to a Dedicated review if usage grows.

Proposed negotiation posture: counter with a 1x monthly remedy cap for month 1–3, move to standard SLA terms (no cash remedies beyond credits) months 4–6, and include an explicit export path to Dedicated/Redeployment if operational patterns require it. We should also request a reciprocal data retention carveout (MediCore commits to documented retention limits for their uploads).

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-amendment-v2.docx (draft redlines)

If you want, I’ll draft a redline to the DPA and a one-page MAP and Marissa can lead commercial response.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Alice Burnett <alice.burnett@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — governance evidence request and a couple commercial questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) SOC2 evidence: attached is a short summary (SOC2-Type2-evidence-summary.pdf). For the full report we can share a redacted copy via NDA; I’ve included a link to our secure DocShare in the email footer.

2) MAP: I attached a joint MAP (MediCore-MAP-v1.xlsx) with proposed dates. Key milestones: contract signature, Azure private listing activation, entitlement provisioning, 30-day verification, go-live handoff. Please review and flag any internal gating items.

3) Commercial / SLA credit: We reviewed internally. We cannot accept an open 3x cash remedy cap. Our counterproposal: a 90-day onboarding credit equal to one month of committed spend (applied as credits during first 90 days) plus an SLA credits cap of 1x monthly commitment for months 1–3, then standard SLA (service credits only) thereafter. If MediCore prefers a larger remedy structure, we’ll need an explicit revenue commitment or deeper contractual guarantees (e.g., 12-month minimum).

Attached are the draft DPA redlines from legal (Redwood-DPA-amendment-v2.docx). We are happy to go into a short call to walk the MAP and redlines.

Next steps:
- Alice: confirm you received the attachments and whether procurement wants the full SOC2 under NDA.
- If you agree, we’ll issue a revised private listing private offer with credits and the MAP baked in and circulate for DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
